title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 3rd Proof The Uniqueness Of Conveying The Message Summoning And Faith

questions.question: What personal quality did he show when powerful groups and even close relatives opposed him?
questions.answer: He showed unwavering resolve and courage, without backing down.

questions.question: Which kinds of opponents are mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Political powers, religious communities, his own people, his tribe, and even his uncle.

questions.question: How did he respond emotionally to that intense opposition?
questions.answer: He did not show fear, panic, or hesitation.

questions.question: What later historical outcome is given as evidence for the strength of his mission?
questions.answer: He overcame worldwide opposition and established Islam in a leading position.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does that success prove about his role in delivering the message?
questions.answer: It proves that no one equals him in calling people to the truth and carrying the message faithfully.

questions.question: How is his faith described in terms of strength and certainty?
questions.answer: It is presented as exceptionally strong, wide-reaching, and completely assured.

questions.question: What failed to shake his conviction?
questions.answer: The dominant beliefs, philosophical ideas, and religious teachings of his time, even when they were hostile to him.

questions.question: What effect did opposition have on his trust and confidence?
questions.answer: It did not weaken them at all.

questions.question: Who are said to have drawn from his faith across the generations?
questions.answer: The most spiritually upright believers of every age, especially the Companions.

questions.question: What conclusion did the traveler reach about truthfulness and deceit?
questions.answer: He concluded that falsehood and double-dealing could not belong to someone with such unique law, worship, prayer, call, and faith.

questions.question: What main subject is emphasized in the first paragraph of the target passage?
questions.answer: His firmness and bravery in delivering the divine message.

questions.question: Why is the opposition against him presented as especially severe?
questions.answer: Because it came not only from large outside powers but also from his own closest social circle.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about his inner state during conflict?
questions.answer: His heart and mind remained steady and untroubled.

questions.question: How does the passage connect his steadfastness with the spread of Islam?
questions.answer: His victory and the rise of Islam are presented as signs of the truth and strength of his mission.

questions.question: What features of his faith are highlighted besides strength?
questions.answer: Its certainty, vastness, and elevated level.

questions.question: What kinds of intellectual or religious systems could not unsettle him?
questions.answer: The prevailing beliefs, philosophical schools, and teachings of religious authorities.

questions.question: What does it mean that later righteous believers drew from his fountain of faith?
questions.answer: Their own belief was nourished by his example and teaching.

questions.question: Who is named first among those outstanding believers?
questions.answer: The Companions.

questions.question: What does the passage say this continued reliance on his faith proves?
questions.answer: It proves that his faith is without equal.

questions.question: Which moral faults are ruled out in the final sentence?
questions.answer: Lying and hypocrisy-like double-dealing are ruled out.

questions.question: In the passage, what two major qualities are used to support his truthfulness?
questions.answer: His fearless delivery of the message and his unmatched faith.

questions.question: What does the mention of his uncle add to the description of opposition?
questions.answer: It shows that resistance came from family as well as from public enemies.

questions.question: When faced with hostility, what signs of weakness are specifically denied?
questions.answer: Doubt, nervousness, fear, and hesitation.

questions.question: How is his public mission described in relation to the whole world?
questions.answer: He is portrayed as confronting the world and prevailing in his mission.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat this achievement as proof rather than just success?
questions.answer: Because such a result, joined with his steadfast character, points to an extraordinary and truthful mission.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the firmness of his belief compared with the ideas of his time?
questions.answer: His belief remained stronger than all competing systems of thought around him.

questions.question: What could hostile thinkers and religious leaders not produce in him?
questions.answer: They could not create doubt, insecurity, or weakness in his conviction.

questions.question: How do the saintly people of later ages function as evidence in the argument?
questions.answer: Their dependence on his model of belief shows that they saw his faith as the highest example.

questions.question: What is the traveler doing when he affirms this with his intellect?
questions.answer: He is reaching a reasoned conclusion, not just reacting emotionally.

questions.question: What final judgment is made about his character?
questions.answer: A person with those qualities cannot reasonably be accused of deceit.

questions.question: What does the passage show about his consistency under pressure?
questions.answer: He stayed firm in purpose even under intense and widespread hostility.

questions.question: Which relationship in the passage makes the opposition feel especially personal?
questions.answer: The mention of his uncle.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about courage by pairing it with steadfastness and firmness?
questions.answer: It presents courage as a stable moral strength, not a brief moment of boldness.

questions.question: What broad result followed from his call to the truth?
questions.answer: Islam became dominant on a world level.

questions.question: How does the passage move from outward action to inward belief?
questions.answer: It first describes his public endurance, then explains the unmatched strength of his inner faith.

questions.question: In what way was his certainty unaffected by the climate of his time?
questions.answer: Neither social pressure nor influential belief systems could disturb it.

questions.question: What does the phrase about illuminating the whole world suggest about his faith?
questions.answer: Its influence and clarity reached far beyond his own lifetime and place.

questions.question: Why are the Companions singled out in the discussion of belief?
questions.answer: They are presented as the leading example among those with the highest levels of faith.

questions.question: What combined features lead the traveler to reject any claim of lying?
questions.answer: His unique law, unmatched religion, deep worship, excellent prayer, universal call, and extraordinary faith.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning structure does the passage use overall?
questions.answer: It lists qualities and outcomes, then draws a moral conclusion about his truthfulness.

questions.question: What does the passage say about his ability to continue his mission despite resistance?
questions.answer: He continued with complete determination even when surrounded by severe opposition.

questions.question: Why is opposition from his own tribe important in the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that the pressure was close, constant, and socially costly.

questions.question: What is proved by the claim that he showed no fear or hesitation?
questions.answer: It shows the exceptional strength of his character in carrying the message.

questions.question: What worldly achievement is mentioned after describing his courage?
questions.answer: He brought Islam to a position of mastery in the world.

questions.question: How is his faith presented as more than personal opinion?
questions.answer: It is shown as deeply certain, expansive, and strong enough to withstand every challenge.

questions.question: What three sources of competing thought are named as unable to weaken him?
questions.answer: Common beliefs, philosophical teachings, and religious instruction from established leaders.

questions.question: How much effect did hostility have on his confidence?
questions.answer: None at all; it did not produce even the smallest crack in it.

questions.question: How do later saintly believers strengthen the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: Their continued reliance on his belief shows that they recognized his faith as the highest source.

questions.question: What does the traveler conclude about someone with all these qualities?
questions.answer: Such a person cannot be a liar or a deceiver.

questions.question: Which two broad areas of excellence are combined in the final conclusion?
questions.answer: Excellence in guiding others and excellence in personal faith and worship.

questions.question: What aspect of his mission is stressed by the words about summoning people to the truth?
questions.answer: He actively called people toward what is right and true.

questions.question: What does the passage reveal about the scale of opposition he faced?
questions.answer: It was extremely broad, including nations, religions, and even close family connections.

questions.question: How did he carry himself in the face of that opposition?
questions.answer: He remained calm, firm, and fearless.

questions.question: What is the significance of his challenging the whole world successfully?
questions.answer: It serves as evidence that his way of conveying the message was uniquely powerful and true.

questions.question: What qualities make his faith stand out in the passage?
questions.answer: Its power, certainty, breadth, and elevated nature.

questions.question: What kinds of outside pressure failed to shake his belief?
questions.answer: Intellectual, religious, and social opposition all failed.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the saintly people of later times to him?
questions.answer: It says they took spiritual nourishment from his faith and saw him as the highest example of belief.

questions.question: What special place do the Companions hold in this description?
questions.answer: They stand at the front of those known for the highest ranks of belief.

questions.question: According to the traveler’s reasoning, what do these traits say about his honesty?
questions.answer: They show that dishonesty and insincerity are incompatible with his character.

questions.question: What is the overall conclusion of the target passage?
questions.answer: His unmatched courage in mission and unmatched certainty in faith confirm his complete truthfulness.
